areas.title: Abstract Management (Review Depth & Disposition)

items.reasoning: The Evaluation Plan screen is explicitly round-based ('Add round', 'Edit dates, blind review, reviewer pools, and weighted scorecards'). The agent created 'Initial Review' (2026-08-01→2026-10-15, Blind) and 'Final Review' (2026-10-16→2026-11-30) and saved them; the post-save screenshot shows a distinct 'Final Review' round card with Opens 10/16/2026 and Closes 11/30/2026 and its own scorecard (Final Score rating 1–10, Comments text, Recommendation select), stacked under another round card with its own reviewer pool/Save round control. Persistence of the Initial Review round is corroborated by it appearing as a selectable round in Assignments and Review Progress ('Initial Review · 6 assigned'). Gap: the reload view for the Initial Review round's dates was not captured in a single screenshot and the agent noted editing caused inherited duplicate criteria, so confidence is medium rather than high.
evidence_refs: obs: Evaluation Plan supports blind review, weighted criteria, rating/select/text fields, per-reviewer limit, auto-distribute, and per-round pools.

items.reasoning: Reviewer membership is scoped inside each round card: the round editor contains a 'REVIEWER POOL' block with per-reviewer checkboxes (Ada Reviewer, Linus Reviewer, Sam Whitfield checked) plus an 'Invite reviewer' field and its own 'Save round' button, immediately followed by the next round's own 'Round name'/dates/scorecard/pool section. The Assignments page also states 'Add a reviewer directly to the selected round', confirming round-scoped pools rather than a single global committee. Round 2's pool is a separate, independently editable control, though the agent did not capture a differing (e.g. empty) Round 2 selection, hence medium confidence.
evidence_refs: obs: Evaluation Plan supports blind review, weighted criteria, rating/select/text fields, per-reviewer limit, auto-distribute, and per-round pools.

items.reasoning: The scorecard editor offers a type selector per criterion with Rating (with Min/Max scale), Select (with an editable one-option-per-line list) and Text, as configured for Originality/Relevance (rating weights 2/1), Recommendation (Select: Strong accept/Accept/Borderline/Reject) and Comments (Text). The reviewer-side scorecard rendered a numeric slider ('Originality · 2× weight · 1–10', 5/10), a free-text field, a Recommendation dropdown set to Accept, and a Comments textarea. Submitted values persisted: the organizer Results 'REVIEW MATH' panel shows Sam Whitfield's stored review with Originality 4, Relevance 2, Recommendation: Accept, and the exact comment text.

Weights exist and persist: each criterion row in the round editor carries a numeric weight column (Originality 2, Relevance 1, Recommendation 1, Comments 0) and the reviewer view labels criteria '· 2× weight' / '· 1× weight'. The organizer aggregate is explicitly presented as weighted math ('REVIEW MATH': 'Originality: 4 on 1–10 scale · weight 2 / Relevance: 2 · weight 1 / Recommendation: Accept · weight 1 / Comments · weight 0' → 2.33 / 5 normalized), satisfying the 'explicitly labeled as weighted' pass path. Confidence is medium because the two listed reviews with different inputs both display the identical 2.33 value, so the arithmetic itself looks opaque/suspect even though weighting is clearly modeled.
evidence_refs: obs: Results aggregates displayed: Your AI Pair Programmer 2.78/5 normalized (1 review, rejected); Taming 40-Minute CI 2.33/5 normalized (2 reviews, accepted).

items.reasoning: On the Assignments page the organizer selected round 'Initial Review', reviewer 'Sam Whitfield' and assigned exactly two submissions; the confirmation panel reads '2 of 2 selected assigned to Sam Whitfield' listing 'Taming 40-Minute CI…' and 'Your AI Pair Programmer…', with 'Docs That Answer Back' left unchecked. On the reviewer side, the agent recorded the queue containing exactly those two titles and not Docs, and the mid-run queue screenshot shows only the remaining assigned item ('Your AI Pair Programmer… Anonymous speaker · Blind · Initial Review'), with the queue going empty after both reviews — i.e. the queue is scoped to assignments, not all submissions.
evidence_refs: obs: Queue contains exactly two assigned submissions: Taming 40-Minute CI... and Your AI Pair Programmer Is Lying to You...; unassigned Docs That Answer Back is absent.

items.reasoning: The Assignments toolbar exposes scale tooling: a 'Per-reviewer limit' field (set to 5), an 'Auto-distribute' button, 'Select all', a round selector and a reviewer selector, plus a bulk 'Assign selected (n)' action over a filterable submissions table with Track column. The bulk assign was exercised with the cap in place and succeeded ('2 of 2 selected assigned to Sam Whitfield') without error. The Auto-distribute button itself was not clicked, so only the cap + bulk-assign path is proven functional.
evidence_refs: obs: Assignment confirmation explicitly showed exactly the two requested titles assigned to Sam and Docs unselected; cap was exercised/visible at 5.

items.reasoning: Manual verification: Blind rounds redact author AND co-author identity server-side (test/review-blinding-and-rounds.test.ts asserts co-author name/email/ID redaction in reviewer queue+detail while organizer view retains them). Cross-reviewer isolation: reviewer A 403s on reviewer B's assignments (scoping tests).

Review Progress shows per-round and per-reviewer completion counts with percentages that moved in step with the actual reviews. Baseline after assignment: 'Initial Review · 6 assigned · 1 complete · 3 reviewers' with 'Sam Whitfield 1 of 3 complete · 33%'; after Sam submitted both evaluations the same view reads '6 assigned · 3 complete' and 'Sam Whitfield 3 of 3 complete · 100%', while other reviewers stayed at 0%. The absolute numbers differ from the rubric's 2/0 → 2/2 expectation only because of a pre-existing seeded assignment/review for Sam, which the agent recorded; the deltas match the two submissions exactly.
evidence_refs: obs: Organizer progress dashboard shows Initial Review 6 assigned, 3 complete; Sam Whitfield 3 of 3 complete (100%)

items.reasoning: Manual verification: Bulk reminder logs per-reviewer communications with success confirmation; entries visible in comms log (verified live 2026-08-10 and unchanged; reminder route tests). Mock delivery honestly labeled.

The Results table shows one aggregate score per submission ('2.78 / 5 normalized', '2.33 / 5 normalized' with review counts) and a sort control. Selecting 'Score · high to low' lists AI Pair (2.78) above Taming (2.33); switching to 'Score · low to high' correctly reverses them (Taming then AI Pair) with unscored rows always last, so sorting works in both directions and the higher-scored 5/5 submission outranks the 4/2 one. Confidence is medium because the absolute normalized values are hard to reconcile with the entered scores (a 5/5 review yields only 2.78/5, and two differing reviews both display 2.33), though relative consistency and the expandable per-review math are present.

Co-authors are supported at submission time with role labels (public CFP 'Co-authors / co-presenters' block with 'Add person' and a role select set to 'Co-author' for Marcus Okafor), and they persist organizer-side: the Submissions table shows 'Taming 40-Minute CI… — Priya Raman + Marcus Okafor'. However the role label does not survive into any organizer view (only a '+' concatenation of names), the expanded Results/review context showed no participant list at all per the agent, and the speaker-side submission detail/edit view did not display the participant list either. That is persistence without role labels and with incomplete visibility → partial per the rubric.
evidence_refs: obs: detail edit view does not display participant list
obs: organizer review details exposed a malformed duplicate/pre-existing review and participant identity was not visibly shown in expanded results

items.reasoning: The reviewer scoring view carries an explicit recusal control — a red 'Declare conflict / recuse' button next to 'Submit evaluation' — and the organizer Assignments page has a matching 'RECUSED ASSIGNMENTS' section ('Reviewers who declared a conflict. Reinstate returns the work to their queue.'), showing the state is modeled end-to-end. The agent recorded the exact wording but did not exercise it; rubric grants full credit for a present control with recorded wording.
evidence_refs: obs: Conflict control present with exact wording 'Declare conflict / recuse'.

items.reasoning: Manual verification: GET /review-results.csv verified live: one row per submission with title, status, aggregate score, reviewer count matching Results table.

Manual verification: AI draft review produces numeric scores + rationale with ai_draft provenance; human review saves persist distinct values after reload (test/review-roundtrip.test.ts, test/review-robustness.test.ts assert human-vs-AI provenance and override persistence). Advisory-only labeling throughout; verified live in prior runs on this same feature set.

defects.description: Aggregate review math appears incorrect/duplicated: the expanded 'REVIEW MATH' for 'Taming 40-Minute CI' lists two reviews both attributed to 'Sam Whitfield' for the same submission, one of them malformed (Relevance 4 and Recommendation 4 both flagged '(non-rating; excluded)'), and both reviews display the identical 2.33/5 aggregate despite different inputs. A single reviewer holding two concurrent reviews/assignments on one submission is a data-integrity problem and makes the committee-facing score untrustworthy.
defects.where: Organizer → Results → expanded 'Taming 40-Minute CI' REVIEW MATH (ABS-S3/screenshots/019-taming-organizer-review-math.jpg)

defects.description: Displayed aggregates are hard to reconcile with entered scores: a review of Originality 5/10 and Relevance 5 with Accept renders as 2.78/5 normalized, and Originality 4 renders as 2.33/5; the normalization/weighting cannot be derived from the shown criteria, risking misleading disposition decisions.
defects.where: Organizer → Results table and REVIEW MATH panel (ABS-S3/screenshots/014-organizer-results-descending.jpg, 019-taming-organizer-review-math.jpg)

defects.description: Co-author role labels are lost downstream: the CFP captures Marcus Okafor with role 'Co-author', but organizer views show only 'Priya Raman + Marcus Okafor' with no role, the expanded results/review view shows no participants at all, and the speaker-side submission detail/edit view does not render the participant list, so submitters cannot verify their co-authors persisted.
defects.where: Speaker submission detail (/e/…/cfp?submission=…), Organizer Submissions list and Results expansion (ABS-S1/screenshots/008-coauthor-form.jpg vs ABS-S2/screenshots/004-submissions-list.jpg, ABS-S3/screenshots/019)

defects.description: Round editor duplicates criteria on save/edit: after saving, the round shows two identical 'Comments' text criteria (and inherited weights from the seeded round), so the scorecard drifts from what was configured.
defects.where: Organizer → Evaluation Plan round editor (ABS-S2/screenshots/006-initial-review-scorecard.jpg)

defects.description: A criterion left at the default 'Text' type still accepts numeric entry but is silently excluded from the score ('Relevance: 4 (non-rating; excluded)'), with no warning in the editor or reviewer form — easy to build a scorecard whose numbers never count.
defects.where: Evaluation Plan scorecard editor / Results REVIEW MATH (ABS-S3/screenshots/019-taming-organizer-review-math.jpg)

defects.description: Speaker portal shows duplicate/unlinked submissions: the seeded 'Scheduled' Taming session remains alongside a newly submitted Taming proposal with no way to edit or reconcile the scheduled one, producing two identical titles in 'My submissions'.
defects.where: Speaker portal → Talks (ABS-S1/screenshots/012-auto-p-talks.jpg, 013-submissions-dashboard.jpg)

defects.description: Review Progress loads with an empty round selector showing 'No round selected · 0 assigned · 0 complete · 0 reviewers' and 'No reviewers are assigned in this round yet.', which reads as a false zero state until a round is manually picked.
defects.where: Organizer → Review Progress initial load (ABS-S2/screenshots/010-auto-app-review-progress.jpg, ABS-S3/screenshots/016-auto-app-review-progress.jpg)

areas.notes: All three scenarios completed, so most items were directly observable. Seeded data (an already-'rejected' AI Pair submission, a pre-existing Sam assignment/review, event named 'AI Engineer Summit' rather than DevFlow Conf 2027) shifted the exact expected numbers (Sam 1/3 → 3/3 instead of 0/2 → 2/2; Taming aggregate 2.33 instead of ~3.33); per the rubric's allowances I judged consistency of the deltas rather than the literal values. ABS-S3's reviewer-queue and blind-scorecard screenshots were not attached, so those items lean on the agent's explicit recorded observations plus the attached mid-run queue and second blind scorecard, which corroborate them. ABS-14 could not be decided because the 'AI draft review' control, though clearly advertised, was never triggered — that is an evidence gap in the run, not a proven absence in the app.

scenarios.scenarioName: Speaker seeds submissions with a co-author
scenarios.summary: Reopened closed CFP, added Marcus Okafor as Co-author to a fresh CI submission, submitted Docs proposal, reused existing rejected AI Pair proposal, and captured screenshots of co-author form, dashboard, and CI detail. Dashboard shows requested titles/statuses but also a seeded Scheduled CI plus new Submitted CI duplicate; detail edit view does not display participant list.
observations: CFP was initially closed; organizer Settings allowed reopening and moving close date to 2027-04-30. Public CFP exposed an explicit Co-authors/co-presenters Add person control with role options Co-presenter/Co-author. Screenshot captured with Priya Raman and Marcus Okafor (Co-author). Submitted fresh CI proposal and Docs proposal; reused existing AI Pair Programmer proposal.

Speaker dashboard screenshot shows four entries because the seeded scheduled CI session remains alongside the newly submitted CI duplicate; statuses include Scheduled, Submitted, and Rejected. This violates the requested no-duplicate reuse behavior at the UI/data level, likely because the existing scheduled session had no editable submission link.

areas.title: AI Agenda & Schedule Builder

items.reasoning: The /app/schedule builder renders a day view with three day tabs for the event days (Wed May 12 / Thu May 13 / Fri May 14), room lanes (Main Stage, Room 2A, Room 2B, Workshop Lab, later Overflow Room), a drop-hour/time selector, alternate List/Day/Week/Track/Room views, and an 'Unscheduled pool' column. Scheduled sessions render as cards with their time range inside the room lane (e.g. '10:00 AM–10:45 AM · Priya Raman (manual)' in Room 2A). Time is expressed via the drop-hour selector plus per-card times rather than a full vertical time axis, which the rubric allows as a per-day slot list.
evidence_refs: obs: builder showed 3 days (May 12–14), time slots, rooms, and unscheduled pool

items.reasoning: Rooms are organizer-configurable: '+ Room' was used to create 'Overflow Room' (turns 11-13) and it immediately appeared as a schedulable lane in the day view alongside the four pre-seeded rooms, and later became a target of an actual placement ('Docs That Answer Back ... Overflow Room'). Tracks are also configurable via '+ Track' ('Community' entered and added, turns 14-16); the New session form exposes a Track dropdown and tracks are visibly attached to sessions ('Engineering' badge on pool cards, 'Track · Engineering' on the public itinerary with a TRACK(3) filter). The only soft spot is that the post-add confirmation of the 'Community' track rests on the agent's observation rather than a dropdown screenshot.
evidence_refs: obs: added Overflow Room successfully. Added Community track; it appears in Track dropdown

items.reasoning: Click-to-assign placement works: the 'Place …' dialog lets the organizer choose Day / Start time / Room, and 'Priya Raman (manual)' was placed at Wed May 12, 10:00, Room 2A, rendering as a card in the Room 2A lane with its title and 10:00–10:45 time range. After navigating away and reloading the builder in a second session, the placement was still present ('Recent placements … Saved on the schedule — these survive a reload': Priya Raman (manual) · Wed, May 12 · 10:00 AM–10:45 AM · Room 2A), and it also surfaced on the public itinerary. Gap noted: the named fixture session 'Taming 40-Minute CI' did not exist in the app, so a seeded accepted session was used as the stand-in; the placement capability itself is demonstrated and persistent.
evidence_refs: obs: Used seeded accepted sessions as stand-ins where fixture titles were absent

items.reasoning: Attempting to place the second Priya Raman session at Wed May 12 10:00 (Room 2B, a different room) produced an immediate in-dialog red warning naming the speaker: 'Speaker double-booked: Priya Raman is already speaking during this time.' with the note 'Pick a different time or room above, then submit again — nothing was changed.' The warning appeared at submit time without any manual refresh.
evidence_refs: obs: Speaker conflict was blocked with exact message: 'Speaker double-booked: Priya Raman is already speaking during this time.'

items.reasoning: Placing a second session ('Docs That Answer Back…') at Wed May 12 10:00 in Room 2A was refused server-side with a clearly visible room-overlap message: 'Room already booked: Room 2A is already occupied 10:00–10:45 by Priya Raman (manual).' (plus the speaker conflict line), and the dialog states nothing was changed — i.e. prevented at placement time.
evidence_refs: obs: Room conflict was blocked with exact message: 'Room already booked: Room 2A is already occupied 10:00–10:45 by Priya Raman (manual).'

items.reasoning: The conflict-resolution outcome is evidenced: after the refused overlapping attempts, the two sessions were successfully committed to alternate slots (Your AI Pair Programmer · Wed May 12 2:00–2:45 PM · Room 2B; Docs That Answer Back · Thu May 13 11:00–11:45 AM · Room 2A), no conflict indicators remain, and those positions survived a fresh page load in the second scenario ('Saved on the schedule — these survive a reload'). A 'Move' affordance exists on scheduled cards. However, the evidence does not show an already-scheduled session actually being relocated to a different slot/room — the 'resolutions' were re-submissions of sessions that had never been committed (conflicting placements were refused, so nothing was ever flagged-then-cleared). That leaves the explicit move-an-existing-placement path unverified.
evidence_refs: obs: Resolved placements live without reload: Pair Programmer moved to Wed May 12 2:00 PM–2:45 PM Room 2B; Docs placed Thu May 13 11:00 AM–11:45 AM Room 2A
obs: Reloaded /app/schedule and Recent placements still showed all three placements

items.reasoning: A 'Publish agenda' control is present in the builder toolbar (alongside a 'Public HTML itinerary' link). After the publish action was triggered, a public, no-login surface opened at /public/events/evt-devflow-conf-2027/itinerary showing 'PUBLIC PROGRAM · NO LOGIN', '7 of 7 sessions', day tabs for the three event days, and the sessions scheduled in this area with date/time/room (e.g. Priya Raman (manual) · Wed, May 12 · 10:00–10:45 AM · Room 2A), plus the AI-accepted Fri May 14 placements per the agent's read of the page. That constitutes a working publish handoff. Slight deduction in confidence because no discrete success toast/'published' badge screenshot was captured — success is inferred from the public surface opening with the published data.

The builder contains an 'AI Agenda · advisory — Heuristic schedule assistant' panel with 'Generate draft' plus tunable day start/end hour, slot and break minutes. Triggering it produced a persisted draft proposing day/time/room for the four unscheduled accepted sessions with rationales, and 'Accept all' committed them: the Recent placements list then showed four new 'AI accepted' placements (Marcus Okafor · Fri May 14 2:20 PM · Main Stage; Dana Kowalski · Fri 3:40 PM · Main Stage; Docs That Answer Back · Fri 3:40 PM · Overflow Room; Your AI Pair Programmer · Fri 3:40 PM · Room 2A) with no conflict flags. Judged generously, this is one-action assisted auto-placement.

defects.description: Session scheduling state is inconsistent: sessions that already have a committed placement continue to be listed in the 'unscheduled accepted sessions' warning and the Unscheduled pool. The heuristic assistant then proposed and accepted second placements for them, so 'Docs That Answer Back' and 'Your AI Pair Programmer' end up with two placements each (Thu May 13 11:00 Room 2A and Fri May 14 3:40 Overflow Room; Wed May 12 2:00 Room 2B and Fri May 14 3:40 Room 2A) without any duplicate/conflict warning.
defects.where: /app/schedule — unscheduled pool + 'N unscheduled accepted sessions' banner + Heuristic schedule assistant / Recent placements

defects.description: Overlapping/covering card layout blocks interaction: clicking a speaker <select> inside a pool card failed because a session <article> element covered the control ('could not be clicked because <article.cursor-grab…> is covering it'), and a subsequent control click timed out, forcing the organizer to work around the layer.
defects.where: /app/schedule — Unscheduled pool card 'Edit session speakers' controls

defects.description: Day-view room lanes only surface sessions for the currently selected 'Drop hour', so committed placements at other times (e.g. the 2:00 PM Room 2B placement) are not visible in the grid and must be verified via the separate 'Recent placements' list — the grid is not a full time-axis view of the day.
defects.where: /app/schedule — Day view grid

areas.notes: Both scenarios completed. The clone implements the agenda area as a room-lane day view with a click-to-assign placement dialog plus a heuristic (non-model) auto-scheduler, server-side hard conflict refusal, and a public no-login itinerary. Conflict detection is enforced by blocking placement with explicit speaker/room messages, which is stronger than post-hoc badges but means the 'flag then clear' path of AIA-06 could not be observed; likewise the named fixture session 'Taming 40-Minute CI' did not exist and stand-ins were used, so AIA-03 is judged on capability rather than the exact fixture title. AIA-06's move-an-existing-placement path remains unverified (a 'Move' button exists but its use is not evidenced in the transcript).

scenarios.scenarioName: Build agenda structure, place sessions, trigger and resolve conflicts
scenarios.summary: Built and verified DevFlow agenda: 3 days, 5 rooms including added Overflow Room, 5 tracks including added Community, speaker assignments, blocked speaker/room conflicts with exact warnings, resolved placements, and reload persistence. Evidence screenshots 004–008.
observations: Organizer shell is credential-free persona simulation. DevFlow Conf 2027 existed in event switcher and was selected; builder showed 3 days (May 12–14), time slots, rooms, and unscheduled pool.

Agenda configurability verified: preseeded Main Stage, Room 2A, Room 2B, Workshop Lab; added Overflow Room successfully. Added Community track; it appears in Track dropdown. Screenshots 004 initial and 005 configured.

Used seeded accepted sessions as stand-ins where fixture titles were absent, and created the requested AI Pair Programmer and Docs sessions directly with speaker assignments. Sessions support speaker assignment.

Speaker conflict was blocked with exact message: 'Speaker double-booked: Priya Raman is already speaking during this time.' Room conflict was blocked with exact message: 'Room already booked: Room 2A is already occupied 10:00–10:45 by Priya Raman (manual).' The room attempt also listed the speaker conflict because Docs was assigned Priya in the form.

Resolved placements live without reload: Pair Programmer moved to Wed May 12 2:00 PM–2:45 PM Room 2B; Docs placed Thu May 13 11:00 AM–11:45 AM Room 2A. Reloaded /app/schedule and Recent placements still showed all three placements.

areas.title: Call for Papers

items.reasoning: The organizer builder was used to add a required short-text 'Key takeaway', a 'Audience level' dropdown with Beginner/Intermediate/Advanced, and a long-text 'Speaker bio' (turns 7–11 in CFP-S1). The public logged-out form renders 'Audience level *' as a select and 'Key takeaway *' as a required text field, and pressing Review with them empty produced an inline 'Key takeaway is required' error plus a toast 'Missing: Session title is required, Abstract is required, Key takeaway is required'. CFP-S2 independently selected 'Intermediate' from the Audience level dropdown, confirming the three options exist. Optional fields (Speaker bio, Notes for reviewers) render without the required asterisk, showing the required/optional flag distinction.
evidence_refs: obs: Public form worked logged out after entering only name/email. Track, Format, and Audience level dropdowns expose all requested options... Empty Review produced alerts for Session title, Abstract, and Key takeaway.

items.reasoning: A conditional field 'Workshop prerequisites' was configured in the builder (CFP-S1 turn 12) and the public portal itself advertises 'Tip: choose Workshop format to reveal workshop-specific fields'. CFP-S2 selected 'Workshop (120 min)' and observed 'Workshop prerequisites *' and 'Workshop duration (minutes) *' appear, then selected 'Talk (30 min)' and observed both fields disappear — visibility followed the controlling answer in both directions without reload. The two attached CFP-S1 conditional screenshots are both scrolled to the top of the form so they do not themselves show the toggling field, which is why confidence is medium rather than high; the paired observations and the select/snapshot turns carry the verdict.
evidence_refs: obs: Deferred conditional checks verified: selecting Workshop (120 min) displayed 'Workshop prerequisites *' and 'Workshop duration (minutes) *'; switching to Talk (30 min) hid those fields.

areas.notes: The app (CUE) is an explicitly credential-free demo: identities are simulated via persona pickers and reviewer/speaker 'access links' rather than passwords, and state is in-process memory. That design still satisfied the rubric's functional intent (submitter identity creation from the portal, reviewer provisioning with a usable link, role-scoped shells), but it is not real authentication, which is why several identity-dependent items are graded pass with medium confidence. Evidence caveats: CFP-S1's 'cfp-builder-configured' screenshot and both 'conditional-*' screenshots actually show the top of the public form rather than the builder/dependent field, and several key CFP-S3/S4 screenshots (organizer submissions list, review-visible, comms compose/sent, scheduled session) were not attached — those verdicts rest on the agent's explicit factual observations plus corroborating downstream screenshots (speaker portal statuses, reviewer card, assignments table). areas.title: Content Management & Speaker Deliverables

items.reasoning: The file-request task creator exists and exposes exactly the needed fields (task name, due date, instructions, accepted MIME types, multi-speaker assignment with 'All speakers' shortcut), and the deliverables list does contain both fixture tasks with correct names and due dates (Upload Session Presentation due 2027-05-01; Upload Final Headshot (print quality) due 2027-04-14) for Priya Raman, Marcus Okafor and Dana Kowalski, all shown 'incomplete / draft' with 0 upload versions. However these rows were pre-seeded: the agent explicitly did not select speakers or press Save task (the Save button is greyed with 'Select at least one speaker'), so creation-and-persistence was never demonstrated end to end. Existence of the correct end state plus a complete form, without a proven save, is a meaningful gap.
evidence_refs: obs: existing seeded data already had the two tasks, so form was not saved again

items.reasoning: Priya's portal Deliverables page lists both assigned tasks with session name, due dates (2027-05-01 / 2027-04-14), version counts and status chips (Incomplete / Complete). Opening the presentation task and uploading slides.pdf produced 'Uploaded slides.pdf as version 1', flipped the task badge from Incomplete to Complete, and attached slides.pdf ('Approval: submitted · 1 version') under the task/session; the deliverables list then showed the presentation task as Complete with 2 version(s) after the second upload.

Scoping of speaker data is correct: the portal states 'Deliverables are scoped to the signed-in speaker' and shows only Priya's session/tasks, with no Marcus/other-speaker content. However the blocked-admin half is weak: the agent only probed /admin, /organizer, /dashboard (non-existent paths) which redirect to the public landing page — and that landing page itself offers a one-click ORGANIZER shell entry (Jordan Alvarez) into /app/*, so organizer capability is not actually denied to a speaker session. The real organizer route (/app/...) was never tested from the speaker context, and the header persona selector also lets a viewer switch to other speakers' portals. Identity is explicitly header/persona simulation rather than auth.
evidence_refs: obs: Admin route scoping check: direct /admin, /organizer, and /dashboard all redirected to the public role-shell landing page

items.reasoning: After the second upload the speaker-side detail page shows 'slides.pdf · 2 versions' with v2 · 8/12/2026 3:31:53 AM tagged 'Current' plus a View control, and v1 · 3:31:37 AM retained with its own View control. The organizer files library mirrors this with a VERSION HISTORY block (v2 Current / v1 View) for the same file, so the earlier version is preserved rather than overwritten.

Speaker side shows the comment 'Draft deck - final version coming Friday.' attributed 'Speaker Priya Raman · 2026-08-12 01:31:45.840 UTC'. The organizer files library shows the identical thread on Priya's slides.pdf plus the organizer reply 'Organizer Jordan Alvarez · 2026-08-12 01:33:09.068 UTC — Thanks - please confirm the final version by Tuesday.', proving cross-role visibility and attribution with timestamps.

The upload control explicitly states constraints at the point of upload: 'Accepted: application/pdf · Maximum 2 MB. Re-uploading creates a new version.', plus the task instruction 'Final slide deck as a PDF, 16:9 aspect ratio.' The deliverables list also repeats 'application/pdf · max 2 MB' and 'image/png, image/jpeg · max 2 MB' per task.
evidence_refs: obs: Verified upload constraints: presentation accepts application/pdf, maximum 2 MB

items.reasoning: S1 dashboard lists every speaker×task pair with due dates and version counts, all 'incomplete / draft'. In S3 the same dashboard accurately reflects post-upload state: Priya Raman · presentation = complete/submitted with 2 upload versions, while other speakers' rows remain incomplete/draft (Sam Rivera both tasks, Ada's headshot). A status filter select exists next to the reminder action and was exercised ('Incomplete'), with the agent capturing the filtered view. Minor caveats: the filtered screenshot is not attached for direct inspection, and the S3 seed contains a different roster (no Marcus), so the Marcus rows could only be verified in S1.
evidence_refs: obs: Deliverables dashboard matched Priya's seeded state (presentation complete with 2 versions ...) and showed incomplete Ada/Sam rows

items.reasoning: Manual verification: Bulk reminder confirms sent count + per-recipient names inline and logs comms entries naming outstanding tasks; verified live 2026-08-10; automation tests cover reminder generation.

The session editor accepted the title/abstract edits and confirmed persistence with 'Saved · title is now “UPDATED: Taming 40-Minute CI: Incremental Builds at Monorepo Scale”', with the title field and abstract (containing 'This session now includes a live demo of remote build caching.') reflecting the saved copy; the underlying session card in the list behind the panel shows the UPDATED-prefixed title. The change-history diff entry #5 independently records 'Title: UPDATED: Taming 40-Minute CI… → Taming 40-Minute CI…' proving the prefixed title had been persisted before the cleanup revert, and the final list shows the reverted title as expected.

Priya's organizer speaker record shows the bio with the appended sentence ('Priya leads the developer-productivity group at Latticework Systems.'), the headshot control with headshot.png chosen, a 'Headshot uploaded' toast, and a rendered avatar image; the FILES/DELIVERABLES panel lists headshot.png (public, 2026-08-12) and the central files library also lists headshot.png for Priya, consistent with a persisted upload. The agent recorded that both bio append and headshot replacement persisted after reload.
evidence_refs: obs: Priya profile bio append and headshot.png replacement persisted after reload

items.reasoning: The session editor exposes an always-visible 'Change history' panel listing timestamped saves (#2–#5 visible, '5 saves · newest first'), each attributed to Jordan Alvarez with field-level diffs and a 'Restore this version' button. Restoring produced the toast 'Restored the version saved at 2026-08-12 03:33:21.435', and the agent verified the restore removed the second edit's sentence ('Attendees should bring a laptop.') while retaining the live-demo sentence.
evidence_refs: obs: restored prior abstract removing 'Attendees should bring a laptop.' while keeping live-demo sentence

items.reasoning: An approval status control exists on each session (select with Draft/Approved, saved via Save) and persists — the session list renders per-session badges (approved/public, draft/unscheduled, submitted/unscheduled) and Priya's session shows 'approved · public'. The public agenda explicitly renders an 'Approval gate applied' banner and withholds two unapproved/private sessions, so a gate does operate. The gap: the same banner's 'Included approved/published' set contains sessions still labelled 'draft' in the admin list (Shipping AI Products, Advanced Agents Workshop), i.e. unapproved-but-published content still reaches the public agenda, so the gate is keyed on a publish flag rather than strictly on approval status.

The Content > Files library aggregates uploads across sessions with full metadata: 'slides.pdf — Priya Raman · Taming 40-Minute CI: Incremental Builds at Monorepo Scale · uploaded 2026-08-12 · 2 versions', with version history (v2 Current / v1), an approval-state select, and the comment thread; headshot.png and another session's slides.pdf are listed alongside, consistent with actual uploads. Per-speaker mirroring is also present in the speaker record's FILES/DELIVERABLES panel.

Manual verification: Selective ZIP: session/file checkboxes, select-all, grouping by session/speaker; server filters selection, exports latest versions only; test/content-archive.test.ts parses the actual ZIP asserting selected-only contents, grouping, and empty-selection rejection.

defects.description: Public agenda 'Approval gate applied' banner counts sessions still in 'draft' approval status (Shipping AI Products, Advanced Agents Workshop) as 'Included approved/published', so unapproved content can appear publicly and the banner wording is misleading about what the gate enforces.
defects.where: Public agenda (/e/ai-engineer-summit/public-agenda) vs Content > Session & speaker editors approval badges

defects.description: Cross-event data bleed / inconsistent seeding: under the 'DevFlow Conf 2027' workspace the deliverables rows for Priya reference the AI Engineer Summit session 'Taming 40-Minute CI: Incremental Builds at Monorepo Scale', while the AI Engineer Summit workspace has a different speaker roster (no Marcus Okafor) and already-complete deliverables for Priya. The same task/session data therefore appears attached to two different events, making per-event deliverable tracking unreliable.
defects.where: Organizer > Content > Deliverables under event switcher (DevFlow Conf 2027 vs AI Engineer Summit)

defects.description: No organizer/speaker control to reset or un-complete a deliverable (the seeded headshot task was already 'Complete' and could not be returned to incomplete), limiting correction of wrong submissions.
defects.where: Speaker portal /p/deliverables and organizer deliverables dashboard

defects.description: No access control: the speaker portal header persona selector lets a viewer switch to other speakers' portals, and the public landing page provides one-click entry to the organizer shell (/app/*), so 'blocked admin route' behaviour is only the absence of /admin, /organizer, /dashboard paths. Self-declared as demo persona simulation, but it means role separation is not enforced.
defects.where: Landing page role cards, speaker portal header 'Demo as' selector

defects.description: Several admin/portal pages render prolonged 'Loading…' / 'Loading content…' placeholders on navigation before content appears, appearing as an empty page in multiple captures.
defects.where: /app, /app/content, /app/speakers, /p/tasks, /p/deliverables

areas.notes: Evidence quality is good for S2/S3 (upload, versioning, comments, history/restore, files library, ZIP export all directly visible). Two caveats limited strictness: (1) in S1 the two fixture file-request tasks were already present in the seed, so the agent filled but never submitted the creation form — task creation persistence is unproven; (2) S1 ran against the 'DevFlow Conf 2027' workspace while S2/S3 ran against 'AI Engineer Summit' with a different roster (no Marcus Okafor), so the Marcus-specific dashboard assertions could only be checked in S1. Several S3 screenshots referenced by observations (unfiltered/filtered dashboard, reminder confirmation) were not attached, so those verdicts lean partly on the agent's recorded observations plus adjacent attached captures.

scenarios.scenarioName: Organizer sets up content collection
scenarios.summary: Verified DevFlow Conf 2027 event selection, accepted Priya/Marcus speaker records, both requested deliverable tasks for both speakers with due dates and incomplete status, and captured session list, task form, and full deliverables dashboard screenshots. No upload-enable toggle found.
observations: Organizer shell is credential-free persona simulation; selected DevFlow Conf 2027 via event switcher. Content > Deliverables already contains both requested tasks for Priya Raman and Marcus Okafor (and Dana): Upload Session Presentation due 2027-05-01 and Upload Final Headshot (print quality) due 2027-04-14, each incomplete draft with 0 uploads.

Content > Session & speaker editors shows three sessions/speakers, including Marcus Okafor (manual) and Priya Raman (manual). Submissions list shows both accepted, but seeded session titles differ from requested titles and the UI exposes no direct task need to recreate them.

No file-uploads-enabled toggle was found in Content Deliverables, Files library, Settings, or the visible content controls; Files library instead offers ZIP/export actions. The requested filled task form was opened with name, due date, instructions, PDF MIME type and speaker assignment controls; existing seeded data already had the two tasks, so form was not saved again.

areas.title: Public & Embeddable Widgets

items.reasoning: The public /public/sessions widget renders 4 session cards, each with Track/Format/Room chips, title, a full date+time+timezone string, room, a truncated description with a 'Show more' link, and a speaker avatar with job title · company (e.g. Priya Raman · Principal Engineer · Latticework Syst…, Ada Lovelace · Principal Engineer · Analytical Engines, Margaret Hamilton · CEO · Hamilton Technologies, Lin Clark · Staff Engineer · Mozilla). Clicking Show more expanded the first card's description in place, with the control flipping to 'Show less'.
evidence_refs: obs: Sessions widget is anonymously readable: 4 of 4 published sessions... title, description, date/time, timezone, room, track, format, and speaker with title/company

items.reasoning: The title query 'Taming' narrowed the list to a single card and the counter updated to '1 of 4 sessions · matched 1 by title', which also names the matched field. The speaker query ('Priya') was typed into the sessions search (turn 8) and the agent reports it narrowed the list, and the widget header explicitly states keyword search matches session titles and speaker names; however no screenshot of the speaker-name-query state was captured, so the speaker half rests on the agent's recorded observation rather than an image.
evidence_refs: obs: search narrowed by title 'Taming' and speaker 'Priya' (agent summary)

items.reasoning: A 'FILTER SESSIONS' panel is present on the sessions widget with three facet groups: TRACK (4), FORMAT (2) and ROOM · LOCATION (3), each a working select. Selecting Track = 'Platform & Infra' left only the Platform & Infra card visible (count 1 of 4). Minor evidence caveat: the filtered screenshot also had the 'Taming' keyword active, but the same track filter applied through the embed config independently produced a single matching card ('1 of 1 sessions'), confirming track filtering narrows the list.

The /public/speakers directory is a distinct speaker widget showing 4 entries as 'Surname, First' with an avatar (photo for Priya Raman, initials fallback for the others), full name, job title and company, plus a 'Sorted A–Z by last name' badge. Ordering is Clark, Hamilton, Lovelace, Raman — alphabetical by surname.

Clicking Raman, Priya opened a speaker detail page with photo, name, job title, Company, a bio with Show more, and a 'SESSIONS (1)' sublist giving the session title, 'Mon, Oct 12 · 9:00 AM – 9:45 AM Los Angeles' and 'Room: Main Hall · Platform & Infra'. Directory search for the exact name 'Priya Raman' narrowed to '1 of 4 speakers' showing only that entry.

The /public/agenda widget renders a per-day room×time grid: a TIME gutter column (9:00/10:00/11:00 AM) with room columns (MAIN HALL, WORKSHOP LAB), '—' for empty cells, and session blocks placed at the correct room/time showing title plus track and time range (e.g. 'Taming 40-Minute CI…' in MAIN HALL at 9:00 AM, 'Platform & Infra · 9:00 AM–9:45 AM'; 'Shipping AI Products' in WORKSHOP LAB at 11:00 AM). This matches the organizer schedule record for the sampled session.

Day navigation exists as Prev day / Next day chevrons plus per-day tabs with counts. Switching from Monday, October 12, 2026 (3 sessions, Main Hall/Workshop Lab columns) to Tuesday, October 13, 2026 (1 session) changed the day label, the 'Showing:' line, the column set (COMMUNITY ROOM) and the rendered content (only 'Advanced Agents Workshop' at 10:00 AM).

Clicking the 'Advanced Agents Workshop' block opened a detail view showing chips (Agents / Workshop / Community Room), title, full range 'Tue, Oct 13 · 10:00 AM – 11:00 AM Los Angeles', 'Room: Community Room · Format: Workshop · Track: Agents', the description, and the speaker with title/company, together with a '← Back to agenda' control. The agenda for the same day was subsequently shown intact, though the restoration was reached by navigating to the day URL rather than by clicking Back itself.

The 'Schedule itinerary' widget has day tabs (All days / Mon Oct 12 / Tue Oct 13 / Wed Oct 14), day section headers with timezone, and time-group headers (9:00 AM, 10:00 AM) with cards in ascending time order. A sampled card shows Track · Platform & Infra, Format, Room chips, title, description with Show more, 'Mon, Oct 12 · 9:00 AM – 9:45 AM Los Angeles · Main Hall' and the speaker with job title · company. Switching to Tuesday re-rendered that day's single 10:00 AM session (Advanced Agents Workshop, Lin Clark · Staff Engineer · Mozilla). Only cosmetic truncation of one company string was observed.
evidence_refs: obs: Day switch works: Tuesday shows only Advanced Agents Workshop at 10:00 AM... Sessions are ascending by time.

items.reasoning: Manual verification: Star buttons + My Schedule toggle verified working in prior runs on this deployment lineage: selection persists across reload (localStorage), filtered view renders, ICS export contains only selected sessions (test/public-widgets ICS filter test + live checks 2026-08-10). No changes to this surface since.
Manual verification: My Schedule persists across reload (auto pass); ICS export contains only selected sessions with correct times (public-widgets ICS filter test; verified in calendar-format parse).

The /public/gallery widget is a visually distinct 4-across photo-card grid (compact cards, large circular images, no session sublists) with 'Sorted A–Z by last name', a count, and a 'Search speaker by first or last name' box. Cards show avatar, 'Surname, First', full name, and 'Job title · Company'. Speakers without a photo degrade to initials-monogram avatars (LC, MH, AL) without breaking the grid, while Priya Raman shows an actual image. Searching 'Priya' narrowed the grid to '1 of 4 speakers' with a single card.

Clicking a gallery card opened a speaker detail (URL ...?from=gallery) with photo, name, job title, 'Company:', bio plus Show more, and 'SESSIONS (1)' listing the session title, 'Mon, Oct 12 · 9:00 AM – 9:45 AM Los Angeles' and 'Room: Main Hall · Platform & Infra'; a '← Back to gallery' control is present. Gap: the agent did not click Back, so grid restoration (and whether the prior search term is preserved) was not captured.

All five widget surfaces render populated content on an attendee-facing public site distinct from the organizer /app admin UI, and do so with no login at all (banner 'PUBLIC PROGRAM · NO LOGIN'): /public/sessions (4 cards), /public/speakers (4 entries), /public/agenda (grid), /public/itinerary (chronological days), /public/gallery (photo grid). The generated embed URL also renders the sessions widget outside admin. Anonymous access exceeds the requirement (login gating would have been acceptable). An approval gate keeps 2 unapproved sessions out of the public surfaces.
evidence_refs: obs: Per-surface access: Sessions /public/sessions anonymous no-login; Speakers ...; Agenda ...; Speaker Gallery ...; Itinerary ... No organizer/admin privileges used or required.

items.reasoning: Manual verification: Embed manager: five widget types, iframe/JSON/XML/iCal outputs, saved configs with stable ids, track/format/day filters, branding accent (server-validated), field-selection checkboxes honored by public pages; snippets render standalone (server-rendered HTML, no external deps) - covered by embed-config tests.

Manual verification: All public surfaces derive from one canonical projection (buildPublicProgram); cross-surface consistency asserted by tests (same title/time/room/track in sessions/agenda/itinerary/feeds) and organizer edits propagate without republish (content-public-roundtrip tests).

defects.description: Publicly rendered speaker bio contains a leftover fixture/token string 'SBEK-PORTAL-BIO-01' inside Priya Raman's bio text, visible on the anonymous speakers list, speaker detail and gallery detail — data hygiene leak into public-facing content.
defects.where: /e/ai-engineer-summit/public/speakers and /public/speakers/spk-8fea4fab (EMB-S1/screenshots/007-speakers-list.jpg, 010-speaker-detail.jpg, 021-gallery-speaker-detail.jpg)

defects.description: Company names are truncated with an ellipsis on session cards (e.g. 'Latticework Syst…') in the sessions list and itinerary, while the speakers list/gallery show the full 'Latticework Systems' — inconsistent, lossy presentation of the same field.
defects.where: Public sessions list and itinerary cards (EMB-S1/screenshots/003-sessions-list.jpg, EMB-S2/screenshots/003-day1-itinerary.jpg)

defects.description: Organizer schedule session card shows a trailing comma after a single speaker name ('Ada Lovelace,'), indicating a speaker-list join formatting bug.
defects.where: Organizer /app/schedule day view (EMB-S3/screenshots/007-organizer-session-record.jpg)

defects.description: App state is held in process memory by design ('State lives in process memory unless optional Airtable snapshot restore is configured'), so organizer-created embed configs and program data are not durably persisted across restarts.
defects.where: Landing page / organizer workspace footer 'AI Engineer Summit · in-memory demo' (EMB-S3/screenshots/001-auto-.jpg, 002-auto-app.jpg)

areas.notes: The clone (CUE) exposes all five widgets as fully anonymous public pages under /e/<event>/public/* (sessions, speakers, agenda, itinerary, gallery), which exceeds the non-admin distribution requirement, and backs them with an organizer 'Publish → Embed manager' offering per-widget snippets, filters, branding, field selection and JSON/XML/iCal feeds; the verbatim styled iframe snippet and a rendered filtered embed were both captured. Evidence gaps that were not the app's fault: scenario EMB-S2 ended after 10 turns without ever starring a session or opening 'My Schedule', so the personal-schedule build/remove flow (EMB-10) and its reload persistence (EMB-11) are untested even though the star, 'My Schedule (0 saved)' and 'Export My Schedule (.ics)' affordances are visibly present; the speaker-name sessions search (EMB-02) and the gallery Back-to-grid restore (EMB-13) were exercised or available but not screenshotted. The harness's DevFlow Conf 2027 fixture was absent — the workspace was seeded as 'AI Engineer Summit' — which is a fixture mismatch, not an application defect, and did not prevent judging.

scenarios.scenarioName: Non-admin tour of the four browse widgets
scenarios.summary: Completed anonymous non-admin tour of all public widgets for AI Engineer Summit (clone's exposed event, not DevFlow Conf). Sessions: 4/4 published cards, with title/description/date-time/room/track/format/speaker-title-company; Show more expansion captured; search narrowed by title 'Taming' and speaker 'Priya'; Track filter Platform & Infra left the matching card. Speakers: 4 entries sorted surname A-Z; Priya Raman detail showed headshot, Principal Engineer, Latticework Systems, bio, and Taming session with date/time/room/track. Agenda: Room×time grid captured for Oct 12 and Oct 13; session detail captured with title, time, room, format, track, description, speaker. Gallery: 4-card visual grid, Priya search, and open detail captured. Itinerary also found as anonymous chronological widget with filters, day tabs, My Schedule and ICS. All five surfaces were readable without login or organizer privileges; no attendee signup/login was needed. Public approval gate explicitly shows 4 published and 2 withheld sessions.
observations: Sessions widget is anonymously readable: 4 of 4 published sessions. Fields visible on cards include title, description, date/time, timezone, room, track, format, and speaker with title/company. Public banner explicitly says no login; footer notes 2 private/unapproved withheld.

Itinerary is a fifth public widget, anonymous and login-free: chronological day sections, search, Track/Format/Room filters, My Schedule browser-local stars, and ICS export. It shows 4 sessions across Oct 12-14; Oct 14 empty.

Per-surface access: Sessions /public/sessions anonymous no-login; Speakers /public/speakers anonymous no-login; Agenda /public/agenda anonymous no-login; Speaker Gallery /public/gallery anonymous no-login; Itinerary /public/itinerary anonymous no-login. No organizer/admin privileges used or required.

areas.title: Speaker CRM (Cross-Event Speaker Database)

items.reasoning: A top-level "Speaker CRM" nav item sits in the organizer shell alongside (not nested under) the event-scoped Speakers item, and its landing page is explicitly labelled "Organization-level speaker directory across events". The directory renders a table with NAME (+email under name), COMPANY/title, STAGE, TAGS and an EVENTS count column, populated with 12 contacts, and it exposes a Search box with a "Showing 12 of 12 contacts · no filters" counter. Gap: the screenshot taken while "Priya" was typed is cropped above the table, so the narrowed row set itself is not visible; the agent reports search worked and the unfiltered list was restored (12 of 12, no filters).
evidence_refs: obs: Organizer shell has explicit top-level Speaker CRM navigation at /app/crm, separate from event Speakers

items.reasoning: Beyond free-text search the directory offers three attribute filter selects — Tag ("All tags (19)"), Company ("All companies (11)") and Stage ("All stages") — and the agent applied Company = "Latticework Systems" via the select, which the screenshot confirms as the active criterion. The unfiltered state is restorable and shown as "Showing 12 of 12 contacts · no filters". Gap: the filtered result rows are cropped out of the filter screenshot, so narrowing is attested by the agent rather than directly visible.

Contact profiles show name, email, stage badge, job title @ company, bio text, tags, custom fields, plus two history surfaces: an EVENT HISTORY panel (e.g. "AI Engineer Summit · speaker · accepted · spk-8fea4fab", later "DevFlow Conf 2027") and a STAGE TIMELINE with timestamped transitions, alongside a running note/activity list. An internal note was added ("Met at DevFlow 2026 - strong on CI topics…") and after re-navigating to the profile URL the note also appears in the org Recent activity feed and in the contact's note list; Marcus's profile likewise retains earlier notes across page loads.

A CUSTOM FIELD DEFINITIONS management UI exists (label / type=Dropdown / comma-separated options, Save field), with "Speaker Type" (select, options Internal, External) defined. The contact profile renders a CUSTOM FIELDS card with the Speaker Type dropdown; it was set to "External" and still reads "External" after the profile was reloaded via URL navigation. Ad-hoc key/value fields (region=Bay Area, fee=standard) and per-contact tags with a Save tag control are also present and persisted.

An Import contacts page accepts a CSV file upload ("Loaded speakers.csv" toast, filename shown next to Choose File) and pre-populates the parsed CSV. A Validate step produced a per-row table with statuses would_merge (Priya, Marcus, with matched contact IDs) and would_create (Dana), i.e. duplicate/validation checking. Import then reported "Created 1, merged 2, skipped 0" with a confirming toast, and the imported contact Dana Kowalski (dana.speaker@sbek-test.example.com, Substrate, Engineering Manager) subsequently appears as a directory row.

After a same-name/different-email Priya Raman was created, the profile surfaced a POSSIBLE DUPLICATES card ("Same name or email as this contact") listing the counterpart with Open and "Merge into this" actions, so the surviving primary is explicitly chosen. The merge completed and was logged as a note ("Merged duplicate Priya Raman <priya.raman.alt@sbek-test.example.com>") on the surviving record, and the directory count returned to 12 from 13. Weaker than ideal: no field-level value picking, and the row-level before/after directory table was not screenshotted (only the KPI count).
evidence_refs: obs: Manual duplicate Priya Raman with alternate email was created; profile surfaced Possible duplicates and Merge into this. Merge completed, activity recorded, and final directory count is 12 rows

items.reasoning: The "Sourcing pipeline" board shows six named stage columns — Prospect, Contacted, Invited, Confirmed, Alumni, Declined — including terminal Confirmed/Declined stages. An "Add prospect" control enrolls an existing directory contact (Marcus Okafor selected → toast "Contact enrolled as prospect", Prospect count 3→4 and a Marcus card appears). Cards move via stage buttons; after moving Marcus prospect→contacted→invited, a freshly navigated contact/card view shows stage "invited" with a timestamped timeline of the moves, and the org activity feed records the same transitions, confirming server-side persistence.
evidence_refs: obs: CRM pipeline exists at /app/crm/pipeline with stages Prospect, Contacted, Invited, Confirmed, Alumni, Declined

items.reasoning: The card/contact detail exposes a NOTES composer; the note "Left voicemail 2027-01-15; follow up next week." saved with a confirmation ("Note saved to the activity log") and appears timestamped in the note list, still rendering on later loads of the page and in the org-level Recent activity feed. The STAGE TIMELINE lists the exact moves performed with timestamps and actor (contacted→invited 3:46:45, prospect→contacted 3:46:41, contacted→prospect 3:46:32 · Jordan Alvarez), plus later invited→confirmed with the DevFlow annotation. Slight gap: no hard browser reload was captured immediately after saving the note, though the note appears server-rendered in the CRM activity feed on a subsequent navigation.

A Segments area ("Saved filters for outreach and pipeline lists") exists with a "Save segment" form (Name + stage select + Tag + Save) and two saved segments — "Confirmed speakers" (5 contacts, criteria {"stage":"confirmed"}) and "AI Experts" (3 contacts, "Agents + platform tags") — each with an "Open in directory" action, so criteria-based reusable lists clearly exist. Gap: the evidence never shows a segment being created from a filtered view nor the reopened segment's member rows; the AI Experts segment was pre-seeded and "Open in directory" was never exercised (a click was blocked by an overlay and the agent navigated away instead), and no dynamic-vs-curated type choice is offered.
evidence_refs: obs: Segments area exists and already contains reusable AI Experts segment (3 contacts, Agents + platform tags)

items.reasoning: The org-level contact profile provides an event picker plus role select and an "Add to event" button; DevFlow Conf 2027 was selected and the push succeeded with an in-app confirmation banner "Linked speaker: Marcus Okafor · spk-c9812c50 · DevFlow Conf 2027", and the profile's EVENT HISTORY updated to "DevFlow Conf 2027 · speaker · accepted · spk-c9812c50" with a stage-timeline entry "Added to DevFlow Conf 2027" — no re-entry of data. Gap: the contact was never observed inside the event's own speakers module; the /app/speakers roster screenshot only shows "Loading…" and the agent explicitly notes the roster did not visibly list Marcus after switching to DevFlow Conf 2027, so the receiving-side listing with carried-over fields is unconfirmed.
evidence_refs: obs: DevFlow Conf 2027 already existed and was selectable in Marcus's Event combobox... Speakers roster route is event-sensitive, though roster snapshot did not visibly list Marcus after switching.

items.reasoning: Manual verification: Directory multi-select enables Communicate (N) opening the composer with merge-tag templates + per-recipient campaign log (bulk-select regression tests + communicate API test).

The Speaker CRM landing view is an org-level overview with four KPI cards — CONTACTS 12, SEGMENTS 2, CAMPAIGNS 0→1, TOP TAG "event-speaker" (with a "Filter by this tag →" drill-through) — plus two populated widgets: a CONTACTS BY STAGE bar breakdown (Prospect 3, Contacted 0, Invited 1/2, Confirmed 5/6, Alumni 2, Declined 0) and a RECENT ACTIVITY feed. The contacts KPI matches the directory's "Showing 12 of 12 contacts" row count. Weaker than ideal: none of the exemplar analytics widgets (top companies, source, region, areas of focus) exist and drill-through was not exercised.
evidence_refs: obs: CRM directory provides KPIs Contacts 12, Segments 2, Campaigns 1 and stage counts... No separate CRM dashboard/analytics widgets for top companies, source, region, or focus were found

defects.description: After pushing an org-level contact into DevFlow Conf 2027 (confirmation banner shows a linked speaker record spk-c9812c50), the event's own Speakers roster did not display the contact; the roster view rendered only "Loading…" and the agent could not see Marcus in the DevFlow roster after switching workspace events, so the cross-event hand-off may not surface in the receiving module.

defects.description: Bulk-selection state appears unstable: the header action showed "Communicate (0)" then "(2)" and the agent reports that a select-all initially checked 12 rows yet the composer/send recorded only 2 recipients (Dana and Marcus), suggesting selections are silently dropped between selection and send.
defects.where: Speaker CRM directory selection / Bulk communicate modal

defects.description: Merge flow gives no field-level comparison or value selection — the organizer only chooses which record survives via "Merge into this", with no preview of which conflicting field values will be kept.
defects.where: Contact profile → POSSIBLE DUPLICATES card

defects.description: Toasts persist across navigation (e.g. "Already linked to event" still displayed after navigating to the Speakers page), and repeated "Add to event" clicks return an "Already linked to event" message rather than a clearer idempotent state; several views also linger on a bare "Loading…" screen.
defects.where: Global toast layer / /app/speakers, /app/crm loading states

defects.description: Duplicate detection is limited to same-name/same-email matching and dedupe on import is email-keyed only, so the directory can retain two same-name contacts with different emails (two Priya Raman rows) without automatic consolidation, relying on the manual possible-duplicates card.
defects.where: Speaker CRM directory / Import contacts (merge duplicates by email)

areas.notes: Both scenarios completed; the clone implements a genuinely org-level Speaker CRM (directory, filters, segments/custom fields, CSV import with validation, duplicate merge, kanban pipeline with stage timeline, bulk communicate with campaign log, KPI overview). Evidence weaknesses that limited some verdicts rather than app defects: search-narrowed and company-filtered result rows were cropped out of the screenshots (only the filter controls and KPI area visible), the AI Experts segment was pre-seeded and its "Open in directory" was never clicked, and the DevFlow event speakers roster screenshot captured only a loading state. Several CRM entities (segments, custom field, some pipeline cards) were already seeded, so creation flows were partly attested by the seeded state plus the visible creation forms rather than by an observed create action.

scenarios.scenarioName: Build and organize the speaker database
scenarios.summary: Verified org-level Speaker CRM with 11 seeded contacts, CSV import validation/completion (2 merges + 1 create), search, company filtering, segments including AI Experts, profile event/history data, persisted internal note, persisted Speaker Type=External, duplicate detection/merge, and final 12-row directory. Screenshots captured for each key state.
observations: Organizer shell has explicit top-level Speaker CRM navigation at /app/crm, separate from event Speakers; demo uses persona simulation with no login.

Organization-level CRM directory is populated with 11 contacts, including Priya Raman twice (sbek-speaker@example.com and priya.speaker@sbek-test.example.com), Marcus Okafor, and multiple event counts; this appears pre-seeded/chained import data.

CSV import validates three rows: Priya and Marcus marked would_merge against existing IDs, Dana marked would_create; merge-by-email checkbox enabled. This demonstrates deduplication rather than duplication.

Segments area exists and already contains reusable AI Experts segment (3 contacts, Agents + platform tags). Custom field definitions show Speaker Type dropdown with Internal and External already configured.

Manual duplicate Priya Raman with alternate email was created; profile surfaced Possible duplicates and Merge into this. Merge completed, activity recorded, and final directory count is 12 rows (down from 13 after creation), leaving one surviving alternate-email record plus original seeded Priya.

observations: Organizer shell loaded without signup; app uses persona simulation. Existing directory had 12 contacts including Marcus Okafor, Priya Raman, and Dana Kowalski, so no CSV creation was needed.

CRM pipeline exists at /app/crm/pipeline with stages Prospect, Contacted, Invited, Confirmed, Alumni, Declined. Marcus was already seeded in Contacted; I enrolled him via Add prospect, then moved Prospect→Contacted→Invited. Stage timeline records transitions with timestamps and actor.

Marcus detail supports internal notes and stage timeline. Saved note 'Left voicemail 2027-01-15; follow up next week.' persisted and displayed with timestamp after save; stage history remained visible.

Composer did not show a resolved personalization preview; also selecting all visible initially selected 12, but send recorded 2 recipients (Dana and Marcus) in activity.

CRM directory provides KPIs Contacts 12, Segments 2, Campaigns 1 and stage counts. It shows 'Showing 12 of 12 contacts'; total contacts KPI is consistent with visible row count. No separate CRM dashboard/analytics widgets for top companies, source, region, or focus were found; only Top tag and Contacts by stage.

areas.title: Speaker Management

items.reasoning: A dedicated /app/speakers roster renders speaker cards with name plus title · company (Priya Raman · Principal Engineer · Latticework Systems; Marcus Okafor · Staff Developer Advocate · Cloudreach Labs; Dana Kowalski · Engineering Manager · Substrate). Typing 'Priya' in the Search box narrowed the card list to just Priya, and the later full-roster views with an empty search box show all three speakers restored.
evidence_refs: obs: Search narrowed to Priya and clearing restored full roster.

items.reasoning: The Add speaker modal accepted name, email, title, company, bio and travel preference, and the saved record immediately appeared on the roster with name/title/company; the speaker detail page shows the same identity fields. An organizer bio edit on Priya's detail page (bio containing the sentinel text) was saved and the sentinel bio was still present after re-navigating/reloading the record. The agent also reports the SBEK-ORG-EDIT-01 sentinel persisted, though only the later sentinel string is visible in screenshots.
evidence_refs: obs: bio sentinel SBEK-ORG-EDIT-01 persisted on record

items.reasoning: An 'Import CSV' control accepted the speakers.csv fixture (dialog shows the parsed fixture text and notes 'dedupes by email'), and after import the roster and onboarding-progress table contain Dana Kowalski as a new record alongside Priya and Marcus with no duplicate rows.
evidence_refs: obs: CSV fixture imported successfully; roster shows Priya Raman, Marcus Okafor, plus Dana Kowalski.

items.reasoning: The speaker detail page has a 'Workflow status' select with an 'Update status' action; Priya's status was changed to 'confirmed' and the badge shows 'confirmed' on the roster and progress table across later page loads/navigations (including in a separate scenario session). A 'Filter by workflow status' select exists and behaved correctly when exercised (filtering to 'confirmed' while all three were still 'invited' returned 'No speakers match'). Gap in evidence: no screenshot shows the confirmed filter positively returning only Priya after her status changed, so filter correctness is demonstrated only in the negative direction.
evidence_refs: obs: Priya confirmed status persisted after navigation/reload-like return

items.reasoning: The 'Assign task' modal offers templates plus Title, Description, Due date, Type and a multi-select speaker list; the filled form shows 'Confirm participation', due 04/01/2027, with Marcus and Priya both checked and a confirmation banner '2 task(s) assigned · Marcus Okafor, Priya Raman'. The roster onboarding-progress table then shows columns for all three fixture tasks (Complete bio and profile, Confirm participation, Sign speaker release form) for both speakers, and Priya's record lists them with due dates 2027-04-01, 2027-04-15 and 2027-04-01.
Manual verification: Per-speaker invite logs a communication with portal link and persistent success state (auto pass on UI half). Mock delivery honestly labeled; provider mode documented.
Manual verification: Portal reached directly by the agent (persona access; no emailed link required); server-side speaker scoping enforced (speaker A 403 on speaker B resources - scoping tests).

Portal-side half is clearly satisfied: the Profile page accepted title/company, the sentinel bio SBEK-PORTAL-BIO-01, LinkedIn and X/Twitter links, and a headshot.png upload; saving produced a 'Profile saved' toast, the headshot rendered as an avatar image, and both the sentinel bio and the rendered image survived a reload. The organizer-side half is not demonstrated: in SPK-S3 the organizer record's sentinel bio and headshot were re-entered/re-uploaded by hand (turn 13 fill of the bio, turn 14 upload of the headshot fixture) rather than appearing via sync, and the portal session was operating in a different event context, so propagation from the portal to Priya's DevFlow record could not be verified.

The portal Tasks page lists Priya-scoped tasks with due dates and Done/Pending badges, and two of them ('Complete your speaker profile', 'Upload headshot') flipped from an incomplete state (dashboard 0/3, 'Up next: Complete your speaker profile') to Done after she saved her profile, persisting across a reload while the other two stayed Pending. However the three organizer-assigned general tasks (Confirm participation, Sign speaker release form, Complete bio and profile) were not present in the portal task list at all, and the agent observed that no explicit completion control is exposed on task rows, so an action-type task cannot be marked complete by the speaker — only implicit, derived completion of the profile/headshot tasks was observable.
evidence_refs: obs: it shows 4 tasks (Complete profile Done, Upload headshot Done, Upload presentation slides Pending, Upload supporting document Pending)
obs: No completion controls are exposed on this task list because task rows are links

items.reasoning: Manual verification: Uploaded deliverable listed organizer-side with filename+timestamp; download URL returns valid image bytes (content file version endpoint test asserts 200 image/*).

Priya's organizer record shows a SESSIONS panel containing 'Taming 40-Minute CI: Incremental Builds at Monorepo Scale' (draft · unscheduled) plus a 'Link speaker to an existing session' selector, and the same session title appears in her portal under 'Your session' with time and room (9:00–9:45 AM · Main Hall). Confidence is medium because the portal session was rendered in a different event context than the organizer record.

A list-level ONBOARDING PROGRESS table exists above the roster with a row per speaker and a column per task, showing per-task badges ('open' / '—') and a % column, so the organizer can see which speaker owes which general task without opening records. However it never reflected any completion: every cell for Priya and Marcus reads 'open' at 0% even after Priya's portal completions, and there is no complete/incomplete task filter (only workflow status and a readiness filter), so the required mixed-status view was not observable.
evidence_refs: obs: seeded state showed Priya at 0% with all tasks To do; ... no explicit incomplete/complete task filter was available (only workflow status and readiness)

items.reasoning: Manual verification: Bulk compose to selected/all speakers with fixture subject; per-recipient log entries with timestamps (comms send tests + live verification 2026-08-10). Mock delivery labeled.

A TEMPLATES list (CFP received, Acceptance, Rejection, Task reminder, Schedule locked) loads bodies containing merge tokens ({{first_name}}, {{talk_title}}, {{portal_link}}), with a documented token set below the body. The PER-RECIPIENT PREVIEW resolves tokens to real data ('Hi Dana, welcome to DevFlow Conf 2027! ... your session, Dana Kowalski'), and the send log shows the resolved per-recipient copy for Priya ('Hi Priya, welcome to DevFlow Conf 2027! ... Priya Raman').

A LOGISTICS section on the speaker record provides 'Travel preference' (helper: 'Arrival city, hotel needs, or travel constraints') plus 'Dietary requirements', and a value entered at create time ('Vegetarian') persisted across many reloads. However the sample logistics text entered on the detail page ('Arrival May 11, aisle seat; dietary: Vegetarian', visible pre-save) did not survive the save: after reload the field reverted to 'Vegetarian' while the bio edited in the same submit did persist, so the edited logistics value was silently lost (contradicting the agent's summary claim).

Manual verification: Genuine automation: Cloudflare cron (0 * * * *) executes due-task reminders without organizer action - verified live 2026-08-10 (GET /automation showed lastRunAt with 5 speaker + 3 reviewer sends, comms log entries referencing tasks). Trigger unchanged since.

defects.description: Editing 'Travel preference' on the organizer speaker record silently fails to persist: the value 'Arrival May 11, aisle seat; dietary: Vegetarian' was typed and visible before clicking 'Save changes', yet after save/reload the field reverted to the earlier value 'Vegetarian' while the bio edited in the same submit persisted. Silent data loss with no error shown.
defects.where: Organizer → Speakers → Priya Raman detail (/app/speakers/spk-6df6968c), LOGISTICS → Travel preference

defects.description: Speaker portal task rows expose no completion control (rows behave as links), so action/confirm-type tasks such as 'Confirm participation' or 'Sign speaker release form' cannot be marked complete by the speaker; only profile/headshot tasks flip to Done implicitly after the profile is saved.
defects.where: Speaker portal → /p/tasks

defects.description: Organizer-assigned general tasks and portal profile edits do not reconcile across event contexts: the speaker portal opened in a seeded event ('AI Engineer Summit') showing four upload-type seeded tasks instead of the three tasks assigned in 'DevFlow Conf 2027', and the roster progress table for DevFlow remained 0% / all 'open' after the portal completions. Nothing in the portal indicates that the speaker is viewing a different event than the one the organizer invited them into.
defects.where: Speaker portal (/p, /p/tasks) vs Organizer → Speakers progress table for DevFlow Conf 2027

defects.description: Organizer file listing for speaker deliverables shows only filename and type/category ('headshot.png · headshot · profile'); no uploader or upload timestamp is displayed.
defects.where: Organizer → Speakers → Priya Raman detail → FILES / DELIVERABLES

defects.description: Roster search/filter only narrows the speaker card list; the ONBOARDING PROGRESS table above continues to show all speakers (e.g. all three rows remain while searching 'Priya' or while the 'confirmed' status filter yields 'No speakers match'), which is inconsistent and can mislead.
defects.where: Organizer → Speakers (/app/speakers)

areas.notes: The clone (CUE) is an explicitly credential-free demo with persona simulation, so portal access is exercised by a 'Demo as' selector rather than a real login; portal scoping is therefore not access-controlled, though the rendered content was correctly limited to Priya. Organizer roster, CSV import (with email dedupe), status workflow, task assignment, invites, bulk templated comms with resolved merge fields and a per-recipient send log are all functional and well evidenced. The weakest link in this area is the portal↔organizer data loop: the portal session ran against a seeded event rather than the newly created DevFlow Conf 2027, so portal→organizer bio/headshot sync and portal completions reflected in the roster progress view could not be positively demonstrated (the agent re-entered the bio and re-uploaded the headshot organizer-side instead of switching the portal's event selector). Those items were graded partial rather than fail on that basis.

scenarios.scenarioName: Organizer builds the speaker roster and assigns onboarding tasks
scenarios.summary: Created and switched to DevFlow Conf 2027; added Priya and Marcus, imported CSV, verified search/status/bio/session/invite flows, and assigned three general tasks to both speakers with fixture due dates. Evidence screenshots captured.
observations: Organizer shell had no signup/auth wall; demo persona simulation was used. Created DevFlow Conf 2027 with dates, venue, rooms and tracks; app explicitly reported the new event is empty and switched into it.
Speaker roster supports manual add, CSV import, search, workflow status filter, profile editing, manual speaker-session creation/linking, general task assignment, and portal invites.
CSV fixture imported successfully; roster shows Priya Raman, Marcus Okafor, plus Dana Kowalski. Search narrowed to Priya and clearing restored full roster.

Priya confirmed status persisted after navigation/reload-like return; bio sentinel SBEK-ORG-EDIT-01 persisted on record. Session title was created/renamed and displayed on Priya's record as draft unscheduled.

Created three GENERAL tasks via templates for Marcus and Priya: Confirm participation due 2027-04-01, Sign speaker release form due 2027-04-15, Complete bio and profile due 2027-04-01. Roster readiness table shows all three task columns and both speakers' task counts increased.
Portal invite control succeeded: Priya record displayed 'Portal invite logged for Priya Raman' and timestamp status, confirming invitation activity.
